text:
Qdrant is a high-performance, open-source vector search engine written in Rust.
By default, it listens on port 6333 for REST communication and port 6334 for gRPC.
It is highly optimized for fast similarity search across massive collections of vectors.

Semantic search (dense vector retrieval) focuses on the conceptual meaning of words.
It uses neural networks to map text into a vector space where similar ideas are grouped together.
This allows you to match 'feline companion' with 'house cat', even if they share no words in common.

Lexical retrieval (sparse search using BM25) is an exact term matching algorithm.
It calculates score weights based on term frequency (TF) and inverse document frequency (IDF).
It is extremely effective for searching exact SKU codes, model names (e.g. GPT-4o, Qwen-1.5B), or file hashes.

Hybrid search merges dense and sparse results using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF).
RRF is a simple yet powerful formula: score = sum( 1 / (60 + rank_i) ) for each retrieval model.
This overcomes the individual limitations of semantic and keyword search, giving the most relevant results.

Product Inventory Release Note:
The new sensor model is SKU-9842-X. It operates at 5.8 GHz frequency with ultra-low latency.
This sensor is designed for industrial automation pipelines and requires the Qdrant database on port 6333.
